messages:
alex: taking the night passback — active issues right now: kv-cache evictions up, embeddings prefetch errors spiking. i'm primary for the next 6h, sam is secondary. quick summary below.

incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - kv_cache_eviction_rate > 2% (eu-west) · 52 affected hosts · triggered 4901234500 · https://ops.redwood/alerts/4901234500 :rotating_light:

maria: quick Q — are customers seeing 5xxs or just degraded latency? any correlated deploys?

alex: customers: ~12 orgs seeing elevated tail latency (p95->p99 regressions) and a handful (~3) reported partial failures for long streaming responses. not full 5xx spike, mostly i/o timeouts before fallback kicks in. no deploys in the last 3h per deploy-bot.

sam: on it — looks like prefetch workers are hammering the KV and causing eviction churn. i've paused the prefetch worker pool in eu-west: `prefetch.workers.scale 0` (rolled back to config store).

alex: mitigation steps done so far:
- paused prefetch pool for eu-west (reduces write pressure)
- increased cache.eviction_threshold to 0.92 from 0.85 (`cache.eviction_threshold=0.92`)
- enabled temporary read-only fallback for low-priority traffic via routing rule `route.weight: 0.1 -> secondary-cache`
- silenced noisy alert for warm-up tasks for 10m (`/alert silence 4901234500 10m --reason "mitigation in progress"`)

sam: logs snippet from a stressed host:```
2026-03-15T02:12:11Z ERROR kv_store: eviction triggered, free_memory=3% key=embedding:prefetch:worker-42
2026-03-15T02:12:11Z WARN prefetch: enqueue failed, rate_limit_exceeded
```

maria: thanks — what's the customer impact status? should CS open a banner?

alex: Impact: degraded latency for non-critical generative workflows (batch/generation streaming). No data loss. SLO risk for two enterprise customers on p99 > 5s. Recommend a small banner: "Intermittent latency in eu-west; mitigation in progress". i'll flag with CS.

priya: heads up — i'll be offline for ~30m at 03:00 UTC (calendar). if anything escalates before then, sam will be primary.

sam: acknowledged. i'll keep dashboards on 1m resolution and push a sticky config if evictions creep back. plan:
- monitor eviction_rate, kv_iops, and prefetch queue depth
- if eviction_rate > 3% for 5m, revert prefetch to 0 and apply longer TTLs (`cache.default_ttl=3600`)
- fallback: move affected traffic to dedicated read-replica cluster (manual toggle)

alex: runbook links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-eviction and internal doc for prefetch flags: https://redwood.internal/docs/prefetch-flags. note: the runbook's auto-scaling step is disabled for eu-west because of recent infra flapping — don't trigger it unless you confirm with infra oncall.

maria: CS banner drafted: "We are investigating intermittent latency affecting generation in EU-West. Mitigations underway. No data loss. Updates in 30m." ok to push?

alex: push it. add the footer: "Contact on-call if you see increased errors" and link to customer status page. :thumbsup:

sam: small follow-up: i've put a temporary circuit-breaker on prefetch requests at the proxy layer: `proxy.prefetch.circuit_breaker=tripped` (manual). will reset after traffic stabilizes and eviction_rate < 1% for 10m.

priya: if you need extra hands i'm available on slack/phone after 03:30 UTC.

alex: thanks team. handoff notes for whoever picks up next:
- primary: alex (pager + slack), secondary: sam
- active alerts: 4901234500 (kv_eviction_rate), prefetcherr spikes for embeddings
- mitigations in progress: prefetch paused, eviction_threshold raised, routing fallback applied, proxy circuit-breaker tripped
- runbooks: kv-eviction + prefetch flags (links above)
- customer impact: elevated tail latency, minor partial failures for streaming, banner pushed

alex: i'm staying on watch for the next 20m then will hand back to daytime rotation unless escalations. will post an update after metrics check at 03:20 UTC.
